decisions.quote: The objective of this article is to assess whether the gains made in pupil knowledge, self-efficacy related to sexual restraint and condom use and behaviour change observed in 18- and 30-month evaluations in Nyanza Province [18, 21] are replicated in diverse regions of the country.
decisions.reason: Both shipped and blind coding agree the study is a replication collecting new repeated cross-sectional data in five additional Kenyan regions to test whether the Nyanza Province evaluation findings hold.

decisions.quote: 18. Maticka-Tyndale E, Wildish J, Gichuru M. Testing a national primary school HIV intervention in Kenya. Eval Program Plan 2007; 30: 172–86.
decisions.reason: Shipped row 61 (DOI 10.1016/j.evalprogplan.2007.01.006, published in Evaluation and Program Planning 2007; 30: 172-186 under the official title 'Quasi-experimental evaluation of a national primary school HIV intervention in Kenya') is Reference 18, which matches blind target_index 0 (cited in the reference list with the variant title 'Testing a national primary school HIV intervention in Kenya'). It was ambiguously paired with target_index 1 (the 2010 follow-up paper, Reference 21) only because Reference 21's title shares the words 'quasi-experimental evaluation ... of a national primary school HIV intervention in Kenya'.

decisions.quote: These results are as strong as or stronger than those demonstrated in the original impact evaluation conducted in Nyanza Province. They support the roll-out of the programme across Kenyan primary schools.
decisions.reason: Both shipped and blind coding agree the replication outcome is successful; the authors state an explicit overall verdict in both the abstract and the discussion ('The replicability of that earlier research beyond Nyanza is no longer in question') confirming that the original Nyanza findings replicated across the new regions.

decisions.quote: 18. Maticka-Tyndale E, Wildish J, Gichuru M. Testing a national primary school HIV intervention in Kenya. Eval Program Plan 2007; 30: 172–86.
decisions.reason: Classify as duplicate (already present in shipped): blind target_index 0 (Reference 18, Maticka-Tyndale, Wildish & Gichuru 2007, Eval Program Plan 30: 172-186) is the exact same work as shipped row 61 (DOI 10.1016/j.evalprogplan.2007.01.006) and was only left unmatched because row 61 was provisionally paired with target_index 1 based on title wording. Reference 21 (target_index 1, 2010) is a subsequent 30-month follow-up wave in 20 of the same Nyanza intervention schools rather than an independent original study.

decisions.location: Introduction objective; TableVIseparately attributed18/30month benchmarks; Discussion/Limitations repeated cross-sectional cohorts
decisions.quote:
The objective of this article is to assess whether
the gains made in pupil knowledge, self-efficacy
related to sexual restraint and condom use and behaviour change observed in 18- and 30-month
evaluations in Nyanza Province [18, 21] are replicated in diverse regions of the country.
decisions.reason: The current source positively distinguishes2007initial18-month controlled findings in40matched school pairs from2010additional30-month programme-sustainability findings in20of the intervention schools, measured through successive pupil cohorts after another12months without booster training. Its objective, TableVIand own-result Discussion explicitly compare new regional10/22-month observations with BOTH these attributed18/30-month benchmarks. Thus2010reports a new tested sustainability-wave finding, not merely another citation/DOI for unchanged original observations. The current source itself supplies this positive design/data-wave/empirical-result distinction; unrecovered2010full body after22routes remains a precision/individual-overlap limit, not evidence that no new wave occurred. Reusing schools or an intervention does not make additional observations/report findings equivalent to2007; complete cohort independence is not claimed. Existing61covers2007initial impact, whereas the separately tested longer-term sustainability benchmark is unrepresented. The closest-chain rule does not collapse these two differently timed findings when the current explicitly tests each; no outcome requested and no outside DOI inserted.
